questions.ask: Do generators write pages into this site: an API reference under content/technical and a changelog at content/changelog.mdx?
questions.why: Yes writes .claude/agent-config.json with those two paths as generatedPaths, so the generated-guard hook refuses hand edits to them. If your generators write elsewhere, answer no and list your paths there yourself; until a path is listed, the guard protects nothing on a docs site.
questions.detect: scripts/generate/ exists, content/technical/ or content/changelog.mdx exists, or package.json has a docs:generate or changelog:generate script

questions.ask: Should CI regenerate those pages and deploy the static export to Cloudflare Workers when a pull request merges into prod?
questions.why: Installs changelog.yaml, the deploy workflow it calls (ci-cd.yaml) and wrangler.example.jsonc. They run your generators under scripts/generate/ and need the APP_REPO_TOKEN, CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN and CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID secrets, so answer yes only together with generated-pages; a site that deploys some other way does not need them.
questions.detect: wrangler.jsonc or wrangler.toml exists, or package.json depends on wrangler

questions.ask: Run React Doctor on pull requests into dev and prod (advisory review comments and a commit status; it never fails the check)?
questions.why: Installs .github/workflows/react-doctor.yml, which runs the vendor's action pinned to one commit, with write access to pull-request comments, issues and statuses, to catch React security, performance and accessibility slips in the few .tsx files a docs site has. The action runs the CLI with its own defaults, which report diagnostics to the vendor's score service. Answer yes only if that is acceptable for this repo.
questions.detect: the site has .tsx files under app/ or components/

questions.ask: Review each pull request with DeepSeek, a low-cost paid AI model (.github/workflows/deepseek-review.yml)?
questions.why: Installs a caller of agent-config-kit's reusable DeepSeek review, with notes about this stack: one comment per pull request from a branch of this repository, updated when the repository's owner, a member or a collaborator comments /ask-deepseek. It reads the diff over the GitHub API and runs no pull-request code. It needs the repository secret DEEPSEEK_API_KEY and costs about ten US cents a review at most, usually a cent or two (the diff and the answer are capped); without the secret it passes and sends nothing.
questions.detect: .github/workflows/deepseek-review.yml already exists, or the user has asked for an AI review in CI

questions.ask: Does an agent need to read an analytics API for this site?
questions.why: Adds .claude/ANALYTICS.example.md, a template to fill in for a self-hosted analytics read API. An unfilled template is worse than none, because an agent will try to use it.
questions.detect: package.json or the site's code names an analytics client, or .claude/ANALYTICS.md exists
